scope: Actual96-run N6 scaled strong-negative reconnaissance; no accepted critical points or infinite-volume curve.
checks: Independently matched96analysis rows to complete native/full-field/harmonic audit records and original fileSHA linkage; no fresh reread/rehash of all96rawarchives.
Independently reproduced means of saved per-configuration maximum Fourier power for every kappa/u/start and compared AF-nematic/vortex/energy/start flags.
Visually inspected scaled-response-check.png: all four initial classes retained, half-mean shading correctly labelled non-confidence, eye guides and no assumed collapse/asymptote stated.
Producer/initializer/audit/replay verification:9focusedtests independently passed9.81s before freeze.
inference: At kappa=-4 vector-max response drops from .227-.242 at u=.1 to .028-.029 at u=.15, remains .024-.025 at u=.4, and recovers .268-.277 at u=1 and .377-.382 at u=1.6. Strong AF-nematic response persists through the dip.
Cold/checkerboard/Z4 show qualitatively similar vector-response suppression/recovery at kappa=-8 and -16, but unit-winding high-C/harmonic outliers are substantial, especially -16.

The observations support competing vector/higher-harmonic finite-box responses and a useful scaled-u hypothesis; they do not demonstrate a universal collapse or a single critical branch approaching one half.
limitations: Most trajectories have few or insufficient conservative time blocks. Do not turn the visual u intervals into equilibrium uncertainty bars.
Four initializer classes with one seed per class are trapping controls, not repeated within-class independent equilibrated estimates.
The maximum Fourier mode contains a finite-volume extreme-value noise floor; harmonic response and coherent mode wavevector must be retained alongside it.
No new N8 scaled comparison yet, no thermodynamic extrapolation, no certified mixing or formal equilibrium phase identification.
Analytic product-box energy probability bound is valid separately, but does not select the dominant low-energy symmetry or prove a phase boundary.
